_about: Cases where the C# port deliberately answers differently from the Python oracle. Every entry says why. A difference that is not listed here is drift, and fails the parity run.

_oracle_adjusted._about: Deliberate fixes the engine has and the Python app will not get (the user's call, 2026-10-24: no more work on the Python side). Taking whole sessions out of the comparison would lose everything else they check, so parity/generate.py brings the oracle into line for exactly this one decision, and the sessions are compared in full.
_oracle_adjusted.climax.no_fake_at_the_start: Segment 0 starts with the session; a fake planned there opened one session in twenty (at the default 5 %) with "I'm coming". The engine never plans one there. Its die is still cast on both sides, so the draws stay the same.
_oracle_adjusted.beat.no_replan_for_the_same_finale: An edge moves the finale marker itself and the climax then confirms the same moment. The Python app replans there, which draws the gentle rhythm behind the pause afresh at full speed - with a climax planned, the edge never slowed anything down. The engine does not replan for a moment the plan already has.

session_files.validate.duration_bool: Python treats a bool as an int, so "duration_sec": true passes as one second. The port refuses it - a session that says true there is wrong, and saying so beats playing a one-second session.
session_files.validate.freq_bool: Same quirk: "freq": true would play at one beat per second. The port refuses it.
session_files.validate.freq_ceiling: The port refuses a freq above 20, the ceiling the settings put on the beat. Python plays any positive freq; at 5000 a note gap rounds to 0 ms, and the engine froze on such a file.
session_files.validate.media_path_share: Python looks for every recorded path. The port refuses a session from elsewhere whose media is not a file on this computer's drives: looking for one on another machine's share opens a connection out with the Windows account's credentials.
session_files.validate.media_path_url: Same rule: a URL is no file on this computer, and handed to the shell from the Session Explorer it would run whatever is registered for it.
session_files.validate.media_path_not_text: Python takes a path that is not text and fails when the replay reaches it; the port refuses the file.

achievements.evaluate.booleans_where_numbers_go: Python's min(True, 5000) hands back True itself, so a bool in a count field reports its progress as true/5000. The port reports 1/5000. What unlocks is still compared and agrees.

settings.read.unreadable_numbers: float()/int(float()) raise on text that is not a number, and Python raises that out of the constructor - the app does not start. The port reads such a value as the default and logs the key. Applies to every case the oracle marks "error".

registry.values.qt_serialised: QSettings keeps a list holding an empty line as a QDataStream blob (@Variant), which the import cannot read. It leaves the value in the registry rather than guessing - the only copy stays - and the engine reads the default. The app writes no such list: tone and rhythm names are never empty.
registry.values.unreadable_numbers: Same as settings.read: float() on text that is not a number raises, and Python raises that out of the constructor. The port reads the default and logs the key.
registry.values.beyond_int32: int(float()) of a number past 32 bits is a Python int the port's int cannot hold; the port reads the default. No setting the app writes is one - the only int settings are seconds and counts.

callouts.draws.session_start: The Python app rolls the talking chance for its greeting like for any line and counts the session's first rhythm as a change of tempo, so a session could open with "faster" instead of a greeting. The engine always greets while callouts are on (the user's call, 2026-10-17) and says nothing for the first rhythm - it only sets the tempo the next change is held against.
